narrative:
The model estimates a 96% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile that strongly align with employees who end up departing.

Three factors stood out as the most influential in this decision. First, your total years of professional experience pushed the prediction most strongly toward leaving. With over 11 years across all roles, you sit in a small minority—only 14.7% of employees predicted to stay have this much experience. The model sees longer overall careers as a signal that someone is more likely to move on.

Second, the fact that you have received other job offers while working here also pulled the prediction toward departure. Employees who get external opportunities are noticeably more likely to leave than those who do not.

Third, your relatively short time in your current role (1–5 years) added further weight toward leaving. This places you with the majority of people the model expects to stay, yet in your specific combination with high total experience it still contributes to the “flight risk” signal.

Taken together, these elements suggest the organization views you as someone with strong external prospects and enough career maturity to act on them. You and your manager should discuss ways to increase your sense of stability, recognition, and growth opportunities here so the role better matches your experience level. Addressing these areas could change the outlook for the future. (248 words)
